findings.reason: Stage 1 removes an optional leftover before disk_write_file creates/truncates and verifies a fresh 9000-byte file. Not an assertion that unlink succeeds; later write/metadata operations are checked.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Stage 8 optional leftover cleanup precedes disk_write_file of sbtest, clean shutdown, and stage 9 content verification. Missing leftover is expected; this is not the stage 9 checked unlink.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Stage 10 optional indbase cleanup is followed by checked O_CREAT|O_TRUNC and checked write/sync. The test needs a freshly truncated baseline record, not proof that cleanup unlink succeeded.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Stage 10 optional indfile cleanup precedes creation of the 12-block file and the exact free-block delta assertion base-13. A surviving allocated file would invalidate that assertion; cleanup absence itself is expected.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd comes from a successful O_RDONLY open in the loop; copy_out errors are handled separately. vfs_flush returns 0 before consulting the filesystem for this read-only description.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Initial fd1 belongs to the console for the kernel-spawned self-test (fd_setup_console). The next open must take fd1 or return 210; this is not the later written-output close, which is checked at line 208.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: saved is an extra /dev/console O_WRONLY open, never the output file. Device close-time flush returns 0. The initial open is not explicitly checked; an unsuccessful optional save makes this close EBADF, but it is unused and stdout is restored by a fresh checked open. Do not claim every invalid saved fd is detected elsewhere.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd is reopened O_RDONLY on /out.txt; the subsequent exact captured-output comparison checks the read. No writable-file flush is discarded at this close.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd is O_WRONLY on /bin/init and the preceding write is rejected with E_TXTBSY. This descriptor is NOT read-only and vfs_flush does not skip it merely because the write failed. In the current boot self-test /bin/init is on the ramfs root (vfs_init + initrd_unpack); ramfs_ops has no flush callback, so close returns 0. Re-review if this test binary is ever backed by WFS or another filesystem.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: s2 was reopened successfully by the checked close/reopen condition at line 714. It is a UDP socket, so non-durable close-time flush returns 0.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd is a successfully opened O_RDONLY /etc/motd used for the expected TFTP payload. Its read length is checked; close-time flush bypasses storage.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: s2 is a successful UDP open on port 5000 after the child exits. Close releases a socket, not writable storage.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Only many[0..got) entries with successful UDP opens are closed. They are socket objects; the failed open at index got is excluded.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: s is the original successful UDP socket, still in use for the transfer until this cleanup. Socket close-time flush is 0.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd was opened O_RDONLY on the permission-test public file with an explicit nonnegative check. This applies to both ramfs and WFS test bases because read-only vfs_flush returns 0.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fds[0] is the read endpoint of the checked pipe for signal-interrupted reads; the expected two-byte read has completed. Pipe close-time flush returns 0.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fds[1] is the matching write endpoint of that same pipe, after the wait loop. It is a pipe rather than a writable disk file, so close flush is 0; this does not certify wait handling.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.source_line: sys_close(2);                                    /* 錯誤訊息不必印出來 */
findings.reason: Only the forked double-free test child closes inherited fd2 to suppress allocator diagnostics. Kernel-spawned self-tests start with console fds; a device has no close-time flush error.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: After the checked close of the O_WRONLY hard-link description, fd is freshly reopened O_RDONLY through name b and the LINK bytes are verified. This close is not the preceding writable fd.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: in is the successful O_RDONLY /bin/echo source. out is the WFS destination and its close is separately checked at line 1905.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Parent closes its write end of the successfully created pipe used to receive the grandchild PID. Pipe flush is 0; releasing it is required for lifetime/EOF behaviour.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Parent closes the read end of that pipe only after a full PID-sized read and a positive PID check. No storage writeback applies.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd is explicitly /dev/null O_RDWR with successful open/read/write checks. Device close-time flush returns 0 despite the writable access mode.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: First pipe child closes its unused read endpoint from the checked sys_pipe. It keeps the write endpoint until process exit. This close cannot report storage flush failure.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: First pipe parent closes its own write endpoint before reading until EOF. Object type is pipe; the exact payload and child status are checked later.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: First pipe parent closes its read endpoint after the EOF read loop. Subsequent content/child-status checks do not establish durability and none is needed for this pipe.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Large-transfer child closes the new pipe read endpoint, retaining only its writer. It is not a reused file descriptor from the first transfer.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Large-transfer parent closes its new pipe writer before reading and verifying the 40000-byte pattern. Pipe close flush returns 0.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Large-transfer parent closes its reader after verifying each received byte; total length and child exit code follow. No disk-backed object is involved.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Spawn-redirection test closes the original pipe writer after checked dup2 to fd1. The duplicate remains for spawn; this operation only drops a pipe reference.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd10 is the checked dup of original stdout from the kernel-spawned console self-test. After checked restoration to fd1, close drops the extra console reference. Must re-review if this test is run with arbitrary redirected stdout.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Spawn-redirection parent closes the pipe reader after its read loop; exact captured text and echo exit status follow. Pipe flush is 0.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Broken-pipe test closes the read endpoint of a fresh checked pipe. The following write must return E_PIPE, independently observing reader removal.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: Broken-pipe test closes the remaining write endpoint after observing E_PIPE. It is a pipe endpoint even though it is writable.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd is O_RDONLY /etc/motd; write was required to fail with EBADF. Subsequent read must fail EBADF after close. vfs_flush has the read-only bypass.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd is a new O_RDONLY reopen of /tmp/data after its original O_RDWR description was closed with a checked result. Full 4500-byte contents and EOF were verified.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd is O_RDONLY /tmp/log after the append writer was closed with a checked result. The following string comparison validates the read, while this close has no writeback.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: The first append write is four bytes one-space; the writer now has a checked close. Later O_RDONLY reopen must yield exactly one two, so a failed/short first write cannot pass this test under the current fresh test-root setup.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: The second append write is three bytes two; checked writer close and exact final one two comparison remain after this call. This exception observes byte content, not a general guarantee that write success implies durability.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd is the checked O_RDONLY open of /tmp for directory enumeration. Read-only close bypasses the whole-filesystem flush even for directory inodes.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd is O_RDONLY /etc/motd during invalid-buffer tests; a successful kernel-buffer rejection implies a valid description in this syscall ordering. This close does not discard a writable-file flush.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd is opened O_RDONLY and validated before enumeration. passwd lookups use their own descriptors. Closing the read-only directory returns 0 from vfs_flush.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

findings.reason: fd is O_RDONLY /etc/passwd and close is guarded by fd>=0. Reading and lookup failure are handled by n<=0; close-time flush is bypassed.
findings.scope: Only this call under the stated self-test/backend contract; not whole-function certification.

limitations: Source-level exact-call review, not new QEMU failure injection or concurrent-writer verification.
Console exceptions assume the kernel-spawned self-test setup.
Writable /bin/init exception assumes the current ramfs root; old generic close rationale must be replaced.
